findings.title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not cover UpdateCompatibilityCheck
findings.body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises the 'metadata' subcommand. The same feature gate (Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES check) was added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run(), but there is no equivalent test that runs `update-compatibility check` without `--features=rolling-updates` and asserts the 'preview feature rolling-updates is not enabled' error. A future regression that drops the check in UpdateCompatibilityCheck would not be caught.

findings.title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code
findings.body: The test only asserts the stderr message via cliResult.assertError(...). The new CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4 contract (and the doc in update-compatibility.adoc which promises exit code 4 for this case) is not asserted. Compare with testCompatible which does assertEquals(0, result.exitCode()). Without an exit-code assertion the documented contract is not actually enforced by tests.

findings.title: Breaking change of RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3
findings.body: Previously exit code 4 meant 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible'. After this PR that meaning moves to exit code 3 and exit code 4 is reused for 'feature rolling-updates disabled'. Any external automation / GitOps pipeline / scripts that branched on the old exit-code 4 to detect a recreate upgrade will now take the new FEATURE_DISABLED branch instead, which is unrelated. Although this is documented in update-compatibility.adoc, this is a silent, behavior-affecting change for consumers of the CLI and should at least be called out in release notes / upgrade guide.

findings.title: Exit-code 4 row in the table is misleading
findings.body: The table row for exit code 4 reads 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled.' In reality, when the feature is disabled the command bails out via printFeatureDisabled() / CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED and never performs any rolling-upgrade analysis. The wording makes the user think a rolling-upgrade decision was made; in fact the command cannot run at all. The row should describe this as 'The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled; the command cannot determine upgrade compatibility.' (The stderr from AbstractUpdatesCommand.printFeatureDisabled already says 'Unable to use this command', which is the accurate phrasing.)

findings.title: Misleading 'Operator will fail' warning when the feature is disabled
findings.body: The CAUTION block states: 'While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' The operator does not fail; in the same PR, UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment deliberately runs scenarios with `updateStrategy == null` and the feature NOT enabled, and expects the operator to still deploy and apply the old/recreate behavior. So the operator continues to work (using the Keycloak 26.1-or-older behavior) but does not recognize the new `update.strategy` field. The warning overstates the consequence and should be reworded to reflect that only the new update-strategy behavior is unavailable.

findings.title: YAML example contains an invalid placeholder value
findings.body: The example shows `strategy: Recreate|<not set> # <2>`, which is not valid YAML and cannot be applied as-is. The intent (that strategy may be either 'Recreate' or unset) is not obvious from a copy/paste. Either split it into two examples or use a non-YAML block to list the allowed values.
